entries.definition: Jerusalem — the navel and heart of the land.
entries.common_view: Commonly taught: the grave or Hades, where Christ lay three days.
entries.citations: (Matt 12:40; Ezek 5:5; 38:12) · see The Sign of Jonah, ch. 4

entries.definition: The covenant identity of a house, consisting of 3 things appointed and provided by its Head: the Word (the manna), the covenant law (the stone tables), and the fruitful priesthood (Aaron's budded rod). A counterfeit Name substitutes a different word, covenant, or priesthood; a Name is taken in vain when any one is rejected, replaced, or removed. A bride takes her Husband's Name by entering His house, coming under His authority, and obeying Him.
entries.common_view: Commonly taught: the person's character, authority, and reputation.

entries.definition: The one complete light — under the KJV's “rubies” (peninim, Strong's pearl), wisdom and the bride are priced above pearls; and the night sky's one pearl is the full moon (keseh, “fulness,” the letters under “throne” and “time appointed”), governor of the appointed times, the one-pearl gates of the city — the merchant's entry at the King's gate.
entries.common_view: Commonly taught: the kingdom of heaven, worth surrendering everything to gain — or the church, purchased by Christ.
entries.citations: (Prov 3:15; 31:10; Ps 81:3; Prov 7:20; Job 26:9; Ps 104:19; Rev 21:21) · see The Pearls of Wisdom, ch. 31
